strings.d1.s0.name: São Bento Station
strings.d1.s0.tips: A station hall lined with 20,000 azulejo tiles telling Portuguese history.
strings.d1.s1.name: Ribeira
strings.d1.s1.tips: UNESCO-listed riverside with colourful houses; take in Praça da Ribeira and the narrow lanes.
strings.d1.s2.name: Dom Luís I Bridge
strings.d1.s2.tips: A double-deck iron bridge by a student of Eiffel; walk across the upper level (next to the metro).
strings.d1.s3.name: Taylor's Port Cellars
strings.d1.s3.tips: A port cellar in Gaia dating from 1692; audio tour with 3 tastings and a garden terrace.
strings.d1.s4.name: Jardim do Morro
strings.d1.s4.tips: A garden at the bridge end; watch the Porto skyline at sunset, then take the cable car (6 EUR) down.
strings.d1.b0.name: Graham's Port Lodge
strings.d1.b0.tips: Vintage port and river views; an alternative to Taylor's.
strings.d1.b1.name: Mosteiro da Serra do Pilar
strings.d1.b1.tips: A terrace on the round monastery; on Gaia hill, with the best view.
strings.d2.s0.name: Livraria Lello
strings.d2.s0.tips: One of the world's most beautiful bookshops (red staircase); book an online ticket for the 09:00 opening (the price counts towards a book).
strings.d2.s1.name: Clérigos Tower
strings.d2.s1.tips: A 76 m Baroque tower with 240 steps; panoramic city views.
strings.d2.s2.name: Igreja do Carmo
strings.d2.s2.tips: Twin churches with a blue-tiled side facade; a 1 m wide house sits between them.
strings.d2.s3.name: Mercado do Bolhão
strings.d2.s3.tips: A restored 1914 market; try cheese and tinned sardines, and browse the upper-floor stalls.
strings.d2.s4.name: Café Majestic
strings.d2.s4.tips: A Belle Époque café from 1921; pricey but worth seeing, on Santa Catarina.
strings.d2.b0.name: Casa Guedes Praça Poveiros
strings.d2.b0.tips: Pernil (roast pork leg) sandwich with Serra cheese; expect a queue.
strings.d2.b1.name: Igreja de São Francisco
strings.d2.b1.tips: A gilded Baroque interior (300 kg of gold); also catacombs.
strings.d3.s0.name: Pinhão Station
strings.d3.s0.tips: The Linha do Douro train from São Bento takes 2.5 hours (along the river, sit by the right-hand window); the station is tiled.
strings.d3.s1.name: Quinta do Bomfim
strings.d3.s1.tips: Dow's vineyard; terrace tasting and a walk through the vines.
strings.d3.s2.name: Pinhão Rabelo Boat Tour
strings.d3.s2.tips: 1 hour on a traditional rabelo boat; the terraced vineyards are UNESCO-listed.
strings.d3.s3.name: Veladouro, Pinhão
strings.d3.s3.tips: A riverside tavern for lunch; try posta (veal steak) and Douro wine.
strings.d3.s4.name: Casal de Loivos Viewpoint
strings.d3.s4.tips: The best view of the valley (10 minutes by taxi); the return train is at 17:20.
strings.d3.b0.name: Quinta das Carvalhas
strings.d3.b0.tips: A vineyard on the opposite bank; jeep tour.
strings.d3.b1.name: Museu do Douro, Peso da Régua
strings.d3.b1.tips: On the way back, get off at Régua for the museum; take a later train.
strings.d4.s0.name: Tram 1 Ribeira–Foz
strings.d4.s0.tips: A 1930s wooden tram runs along the river to the Atlantic; board at the Infante stop.
strings.d4.s1.name: Foz do Douro Lighthouse
strings.d4.s1.tips: Lighthouse and crashing waves; see the Pérgola seafront columns.
strings.d4.s2.name: Praia dos Ingleses and Seafront
strings.d4.s2.tips: Foz beaches and cafés; swim in summer (the Atlantic is cold).
strings.d4.s3.name: Casa de Pasto da Palmeira, Foz
strings.d4.s3.tips: Small plates with a sea view; modern Portuguese cooking.
strings.d4.s4.name: Palácio de Cristal Gardens
strings.d4.s4.tips: Terraced gardens with peacocks; views of the river and bridge, bus 500.
strings.d4.b0.name: Serralves Museum
strings.d4.b0.tips: Siza's contemporary art museum and an Art Deco villa in a park; an alternative to the Crystal Palace.
strings.d4.b1.name: Brasão Cervejaria Foz
strings.d4.b1.tips: Francesinha (Porto's "heart attack" sandwich) with its sauce.
strings.d5.s0.name: Guimarães Castle
strings.d5.s0.tips: 1 hour by train; a 10th-century castle, the "birthplace of Portugal".
strings.d5.s1.name: Palace of the Dukes of Braganza
strings.d5.s1.tips: A Burgundian-style ducal palace; look out for the tapestries.
strings.d5.s2.name: Largo da Oliveira, Guimarães
strings.d5.s2.tips: A UNESCO medieval square; lunch at Cor de Tangerina.
strings.d5.s3.name: Bom Jesus do Monte, Braga
strings.d5.s3.tips: Take the bus or train to Braga; a Baroque zigzag staircase of 577 steps and a water-powered funicular (1882), with views.
strings.d5.s4.name: Braga Cathedral
strings.d5.s4.tips: Portugal's oldest cathedral; then the train back.
strings.d5.b0.name: Santuário do Sameiro
strings.d5.b0.tips: A sanctuary above Bom Jesus; views.
strings.d5.b1.name: Frigideiras do Cantinho, Braga
strings.d5.b1.tips: A café dating from 1796; try the frigideira pastry.
strings.d6.s0.name: Aveiro Moliceiro Boat
strings.d6.s0.tips: 1 hour by train; canal boats in the "Venice of Portugal" (45 minutes), plus Art Nouveau houses.
strings.d6.s1.name: Confeitaria Peixinho
strings.d6.s1.tips: A pastry shop from 1856; try ovos moles (egg-yolk sweets in shell shapes).
strings.d6.s2.name: Costa Nova Striped Houses
strings.d6.s2.tips: 30 minutes by bus; candy-striped fishermen's houses (palheiros) and a beach.
strings.d6.s3.name: Dóri, Costa Nova
strings.d6.s3.tips: A lagoon-side fish restaurant for lunch; try the caldeirada (fish stew).
strings.d6.s4.name: Praia da Costa Nova
strings.d6.s4.tips: Atlantic beach and dunes; then head back.
strings.d6.b0.name: Vista Alegre Factory
strings.d6.b0.tips: A porcelain factory museum; in Ílhavo.
strings.d6.b1.name: Salpoente Aveiro
strings.d6.b1.tips: A bacalhau (salt cod) tasting menu in a salt warehouse.
strings.d7.s0.name: Rua de Miguel Bombarda Galleries
strings.d7.s0.tips: A street of art galleries; Centro Comercial Bombarda for design.
strings.d7.s1.name: Cedofeita Neighbourhood
strings.d7.s2.name: Manteigaria Porto
strings.d7.s2.tips: Warm pastel de nata (custard tart); near Clérigos.
strings.d7.s3.name: Rua das Flores
strings.d7.s3.tips: A pedestrian street; say goodbye with Casa Portuguesa do Pastel de Bacalhau.
strings.d7.s4.name: Trindade Metro to the Airport
strings.d7.b0.name: Bonjardim Grill
strings.d7.b0.tips: A street-side restaurant serving piri piri chicken.
strings.d7.b1.name: Casa da Música
strings.d7.b1.tips: Koolhaas's white concrete concert hall; tour at 11:00, an alternative to the galleries.
strings.note0: Andante 24-hour pass 7 EUR (metro and bus); metro line E to the airport takes 30 minutes. Take CP trains to Douro, Guimarães and Aveiro (book online; right-hand window for the Douro). The hills are steep.
strings.note1: Summer is 25-30°C; São João night falls on 23 June (plastic hammers, fireworks), the Douro vineyards are green, and the Foz beaches are open (Atlantic 18°C).
strings.note2: Francesinha 12-15, pastel 1.30, port tasting 20-25, Lello 10 (counts towards a book), coffee 1; tip by rounding up.
strings.note3: Book Lello online for 09:00; do Clérigos in the morning; the Douro train is full on summer weekends, so book ahead; Bolhão market is closed.
strings.note4: Tripas à moda do Porto (tripe; locals are nicknamed 'tripeiros'), bacalhau, francesinha, vinho verde, tawny and ruby port.
strings.note5: Ribeira is safe at night; Gaia cellars close at 17:00.
strings.transit.name: Andante 24-hour pass
strings.transit.why_chosen: Metro, bus and tram; includes metro line E to the airport
